reportContent:
# Plan: EvalKit SDK beta release polish (DX review)

## Context

EvalKit is a Python SDK for ML engineers evaluating LLM responses. The beta
release plan (PLAN.md) ships the current SDK contracts unchanged. This review
runs /plan-devex-review in DX POLISH mode against the documented contracts in
README.md, docs/current-contracts.md, docs/api.md, docs/benchmarks.md, and
docs/package-contents.txt, and records which contracts the beta should repair.

Settled inputs (from the repo, not re-asked):
- Persona: ML engineer, writes Python daily, terminal-first (README.md:3-5)
- Target: first real result in under 2 minutes (docs/benchmarks.md:8)
- Magical-moment vehicle: `python -m evalkit.demo` terminal demo (README.md:14-17)
- Mode: DX POLISH, existing release scope (README.md:5-6, PLAN.md)
- Product type: Library/SDK (Python package on PyPI)

Setup decisions made in this session:
- D0: Add gstack skill routing rules to CLAUDE.md. Deferred until plan mode
  exits (plan mode allows edits to this file only). Post-review step: append
  the routing section to CLAUDE.md and commit it.
- D1: Skipped /office-hours; the inputs it would produce are already documented.

## Developer Persona Card

```
TARGET DEVELOPER PERSONA
========================
Who:       ML engineer evaluating LLM responses, writes Python daily
Context:   Terminal session, wants a local eval result before wiring the SDK
           into production CI
Tolerance: Under 2 minutes to first real result (agreed target); peers land
           in 2-4 minutes, so anything past ~5 minutes reads as broken
Expects:   pip install, one command, real scores on screen; a key step only
           when they go live; errors that say what to change
```

## Competitive DX Benchmark

Source: docs/benchmarks.md internal study (same developer, same machine,
measured from before install to first real evaluation result). Web research
unavailable in this session (Aside not installed); reference tiers are the
skill's built-in Stripe/Vercel/Firebase/Docker benchmarks.

```
COMPETITIVE DX BENCHMARK
=========================
Tool           | TTHW   | Notable DX choice                          | Source
Peer SDK A     | 2 min  | No first-run gate; result on first command | docs/benchmarks.md
Peer SDK C     | 3 min  |                                             | docs/benchmarks.md
Peer SDK B     | 4 min  |                                             | docs/benchmarks.md
EvalKit (now)  | 6 min  | 5 of 6 minutes is the mandatory CI wait     | docs/benchmarks.md
EvalKit target | <2 min | Champion tier (agreed)                      | docs/benchmarks.md:8
```

## Developer Empathy Narrative (confirmed, D2)

I'm an ML engineer with a notebook full of LLM outputs I need to score. I open
the README. Install is one line, `python -m pip install evalkit==2.0.0b1`,
fine. Next line says run `python examples/first_eval.py`. I run it: No such
file or directory. The package inventory confirms that file isn't shipped
anywhere. Thirty seconds in and the quickstart is already wrong. I read on and
find `python -m evalkit.demo`. I run it. It prints "Verifying the
sample-project binding with EvalKit CI; inspect
https://ci.evalkit.example/checks/<id>; normally completes within 300s." Then a
stderr line every 30 seconds: "Waiting for CI check: 90s elapsed of 300s."
Five minutes for a keyless demo of bundled sample data. Peer SDK A gave me a
real score in two minutes total. I alt-tab and half forget about it. When it
finally prints example scores, I'm mildly pleased but wary. I create a key,
export EVALKIT_API_KEY, mistype one character, and get
`AuthError("request failed")`. No code, no cause, no hint it was the key. I
open docs/api.md to write my first real call and see
`run_eval(dataset, evaluator)` next to `run_batch(evaluator, dataset)`,
reversed positional order, no keyword requirement. I know I'll swap them at
least once. And I notice my v1 scripts calling `Client.evaluate()` will simply
break on v2 with no alias or warning.

## Friction Point Decisions (Step 0F)

### D3. First-run CI gate (Hello World) — DECIDED: move the check off first-run
- Evidence: docs/current-contracts.md:3-5 (mandatory 300s remote CI check on
  every first local evaluation, no skip, no offline path); docs/benchmarks.md
  (6 min measured, 5 min is the wait; target < 2 min).
- Change: `python -m evalkit.demo` and the first local `run_eval` return
  immediately using the shipped mock transport / offline sample data. The
  sample-project binding check moves to the first live (keyed) evaluation and
  to noninteractive CI mode. The existing progress line, pre-countdown
  explanation, EVALKIT_CI_TIMEOUT message, and help link are retained verbatim
  at the new location.
- Docs to update: README.md:17-23 (remove "waits for the mandatory CI check"
  from the demo description), docs/current-contracts.md:3-10.
- Coordination: runtime is maintained separately (README.md:39-40); the plan
  must name the runtime change as a beta dependency, not assume it.
- Expected effect: TTHW from 6 min to roughly 1 min (install ~30s, demo ~10s).

### D4. Quickstart points at a missing file (Hello World) — DECIDED: demo first, ship first_eval.py too
- Evidence: README.md:11 references examples/first_eval.py; docs/package-contents.txt:8-9
  says it is absent from the wheel and the examples archive.
- Change: README quickstart step 2 becomes `python -m evalkit.demo` with the
  expected output block (README.md:34-36) shown right under it. Step 3 is
  `python examples/first_eval.py`, a real dataset + evaluator + `run_eval`
  call that ships in both the package and the examples archive, with its own
  expected output. Add a release check that the example is present in both
  artifacts.

### D5. Reversed positional order in run_eval / run_batch (Real Usage) — DECIDED: same order, keyword-only
- Evidence: docs/api.md:5-9.
- Change: both signatures become `run_eval(*, dataset, evaluator)` and
  `run_batch(*, dataset, evaluator)` (keyword-only; positional use raises a
  TypeError that names both parameters and shows the corrected call). Update
  docs/api.md, README example, examples/first_eval.py, and docstrings to the
  keyword form. List run_batch's order change in the 2.0 changelog and the
  migration guide (see D7).

### D6. AuthError("request failed") (Debug) — DECIDED: code + cause + fix + docs link
- Evidence: docs/api.md:11-13; contrast docs/current-contracts.md:21-24 (every
  other error already has cause, argument, fix, redaction).
- Change: `AuthError` carries `code` (EVALKIT_AUTH_MISSING_KEY when
  EVALKIT_API_KEY is unset/empty; EVALKIT_AUTH_INVALID_KEY when rejected;
  EVALKIT_AUTH_REVOKED_KEY when the console reports revoked), a message that
  names the cause and the fix ("Set EVALKIT_API_KEY" or "Create or rotate a key
  at https://console.evalkit.example/settings/api-keys, then export it"), a
  masked key suffix only (never the full key), and a help URL per code. Add
  the codes to the API reference alongside EVALKIT_CI_TIMEOUT. Update
  docs/api.md:11-13.

### D7. Client.evaluate() removed without alias (Upgrade) — DECIDED: alias + warning + guide + codemod
- Evidence: docs/api.md:15-18.
- Change: keep `Client.evaluate()` as a thin alias for `Client.run()` that
  emits `DeprecationWarning("Client.evaluate() is deprecated and will be
  removed in <version>; use Client.run()")` once per process. Write
  docs/migrating-v1-to-v2.md covering: the rename, the run_batch argument
  order change (D5), the AuthError codes (D6), the first-run behavior change
  (D3). Ship a codemod (`python -m evalkit.codemod v1-to-v2 <path>` or an
  equivalent documented sed recipe) with a test fixture. Changelog gains a
  "Breaking changes" block naming both changes and the alias removal version.

## Developer Journey Map (after 0F)

```
STAGE           | DEVELOPER DOES                         | FRICTION POINTS                         | STATUS
----------------|----------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|--------
1. Discover     | Reads README.md intro                  | none; persona and value stated in 3 lines| ok
2. Install      | python -m pip install evalkit==2.0.0b1 | none; one command, Py3.10+, no Docker    | ok
3. Hello World  | python -m evalkit.demo                 | D4 quickstart pointed at missing file    | fixed
                |                                        | D3 5-minute CI gate before any output    | fixed
4. Real Usage   | key -> export -> run_eval(...)         | D5 reversed positional order             | fixed
5. Debug        | Bad key on first live call             | D6 AuthError("request failed")           | fixed
6. Upgrade      | pip install -U from v1                 | D7 hard removal of Client.evaluate()     | fixed
```

## First-Time Developer Confusion Report (confirmed, D8: address all)

```
FIRST-TIME DEVELOPER REPORT
============================
Persona: ML engineer, Python daily, terminal-first
Attempting: EvalKit 2.0.0b1 getting started (current contracts)

CONFUSION LOG:
T+0:00  README, pip install. Works.                                        (#0 none)
T+0:30  python examples/first_eval.py -> No such file. "Is my install     (#1 -> D4, addressed)
        broken?" README.md:11 vs docs/package-contents.txt:8
T+1:00  python -m evalkit.demo -> "Verifying the sample-project binding    (#2 -> D3, addressed)
        with EvalKit CI... normally completes within 300s." Why does a
        keyless demo on bundled data need remote CI?
T+1:30  "Waiting for CI check: 30s elapsed of 300s". Alt-tabs away.       (#2 cont.)
T+6:00  Scores print. Creates key, exports with a typo. First live call:  (#3 -> D6, addressed)
        AuthError("request failed"). Network? SDK? My code?
T+8:00  Writes run_batch in run_eval's argument order. Wrong result or    (#4 -> D5, addressed)
        type error, unsure which.
T+9:00  Old v1 script: AttributeError on Client.evaluate. No warning,     (#5 -> D7, addressed)
        no guide.
T+9:30  Final state: succeeded, 9.5 min, five "is it me?" moments,
        against a 2-minute target.
```

## Review Pass Findings

### Pass 1: Getting Started — 3/10 -> 9/10
- Before: TTHW 6 min (target < 2), first quickstart command fails.
- Fixed by D3 (CI gate off first-run), D4 (quickstart order + shipped example).
- D10 (new, DECIDED): demo prints a next-step footer after the overall score:
  `Next: create a key at https://console.evalkit.example/settings/api-keys,
  then run: export EVALKIT_API_KEY=... && python examples/first_eval.py`.
  Skip the key line when EVALKIT_API_KEY is already set. Update README.md:34-36
  and the demo output fixture.
- Ideal sequence (3 steps, ~1 min): pip install (~30s) -> python -m evalkit.demo
  (~10s, scores + next step) -> export key + python examples/first_eval.py.
- Remaining gap to 10: key creation still requires a browser visit; acceptable
  for a live call, out of POLISH scope to change.

### Pass 2: API/SDK Design — 4/10 -> 8/10
- Fixed by D5. Retained: bounded timeouts, retries, rate limits, idempotent
  evaluation IDs (docs/current-contracts.md:23-24). No further issues.

### Pass 3: Error Messages — 5/10 -> 9/10
- Traced: (1) invalid key: `AuthError("request failed")` -> D6 tiered codes.
  (2) CI timeout: already Rust-tier (code, URL, help link) and retained at its
  new location under D3. (3) swapped run_batch args: silent/opaque -> D5
  keyword-only TypeError naming both parameters. No further issues.

### Pass 4: Documentation — 4/10 -> 8/10
- Fixed by D4 (quickstart), D7 (migration guide), D3 (README.md:17-23 and
  docs/current-contracts.md:3-10 rewritten). Docs are version-pinned to
  2.0.0b1. No further issues.

### Pass 5: Upgrade Path — 2/10 -> 9/10
- Fixed by D7 (alias, DeprecationWarning, guide, codemod, removal version in
  changelog). No further issues.

### Pass 6: Developer Environment — 9/10 (no change)
- Python 3.10+, macOS/Linux/Windows, no Docker, type annotations, mock
  transport, offline sample data, noninteractive CI mode all exist
  (docs/current-contracts.md:26-28). No issues.

### Pass 7: Community & Ecosystem — 7/10 (no change)
- Support contact, changelog, contributor guide exist. No community program
  proposed; correct for POLISH scope. No issues.

### Pass 8: DX Measurement — 6/10 -> 9/10
- Existing: timing instrumentation and post-beta survey (docs/benchmarks.md:9-10).
- D11 (new, DECIDED): repeat the docs/benchmarks.md protocol on the 2.0.0b1
  release candidate with D3, D4, D10 applied; record the measured TTHW in
  docs/benchmarks.md beside the 6-minute baseline. Release gate: under 2
  minutes or the beta waits. Gives /devex-review a real post-ship baseline.

### Outside voice
Codex review skipped (codex_reviews disabled). Re-enable:
`gstack-config set codex_reviews enabled`. No substitute reviewer was run;
outside coverage for this plan is recorded as disabled.

## Magical Moment Specification

Vehicle: copy-paste terminal demo, `python -m evalkit.demo`, keyless, uses the
shipped mock transport and bundled sample_responses.json, prints per-example
scores and an overall score (README.md:31-36). Already in the package
(docs/package-contents.txt). Blocker to the moment: the demo waits on the
mandatory 5-minute remote CI check before printing anything useful.

Implementation requirements after this review:
- D3: demo returns immediately; no CI check on the keyless path.
- D10: demo output ends with a next-step footer pointing at key creation and
  `python examples/first_eval.py`.
- Documented output (README.md:34-36) updated to the new five-line form and
  covered by the demo output test fixture.

## Competitive DX Benchmark (post-review)

```
Tool           | TTHW        | Notes
Peer SDK A     | 2 min       | measured, docs/benchmarks.md
Peer SDK C     | 3 min       | measured
Peer SDK B     | 4 min       | measured
EvalKit before | 6 min       | measured; 5 min is the first-run CI wait
EvalKit after  | ~1 min est. | D3 + D4 + D10; MUST be measured per D11 before beta
```

## NOT in scope (considered, deferred)

- Hosted playground / browser sandbox: persona is terminal-first and the
  terminal demo is the approved vehicle (README.md:14-17).
- In-terminal key provisioning (`evalkit login`): would remove the one
  remaining browser visit, but adds an auth flow to a POLISH release.
- Additional language bindings, community program, new hosted service:
  excluded by docs/current-contracts.md:29-30.
- Consolidating `Client.run()` with `run_eval`/`run_batch` naming: no evidence
  in the docs of what differs; revisit after beta feedback.

## What already exists (reuse, do not rebuild)

- Mock transport and offline sample data (docs/current-contracts.md:27) carry
  the keyless demo and first local eval under D3.
- Noninteractive CI mode (docs/current-contracts.md:27) is the natural home
  for the sample-project binding check moved by D3.
- CI timeout error format: code + URL + help link (docs/current-contracts.md:15-18)
  is the template for the D6 AuthError codes.
- Secret redaction in errors (docs/current-contracts.md:22) applies to the
  masked key suffix in D6.
- Timing instrumentation and survey (docs/benchmarks.md:9-10) power D11.
- Changelog, API reference, contributor guide, support contact exist;
  D5/D6/D7 add entries rather than new documents, except the migration guide.

## TODOS.md updates

- D12 (accepted): **Remove `Client.evaluate()` alias.** What: delete the
  alias and DeprecationWarning at the version named in the 2.0 changelog.
  Why: one public name per action; keeps the warning honest. Pros: clean
  surface. Cons: stragglers break at that version (the notice period is the
  mitigation). Context: alias in evalkit/client.py; remediation is
  docs/migrating-v1-to-v2.md and the codemod. Depends on: D7 shipped in
  2.0.0b1, changelog names the removal version. Written to TODOS.md when
  plan mode exits.

## DX Scorecard

```
+====================================================================+
|              DX PLAN REVIEW — SCORECARD                             |
+====================================================================+
| Dimension            | Score  | Prior  | Trend  |
|----------------------|--------|--------|--------|
| Getting Started      |  9/10  |  3/10  | +6 ↑   |
| API/CLI/SDK          |  8/10  |  4/10  | +4 ↑   |
| Error Messages       |  9/10  |  5/10  | +4 ↑   |
| Documentation        |  8/10  |  4/10  | +4 ↑   |
| Upgrade Path         |  9/10  |  2/10  | +7 ↑   |
| Dev Environment      |  9/10  |  9/10  |  0 =   |
| Community            |  7/10  |  7/10  |  0 =   |
| DX Measurement       |  9/10  |  6/10  | +3 ↑   |
```
